Issued at 300 AM EDT Fri Aug 14 2026

Currently-Tonight... KMLB radar imagery shows dry conditions over 
east central Florida. GOES-19 satellite imagery and local 
observations indicate clear to partly cloudy skies. Temperatures are 
currently in the mid 70s to low 80s with dew points in the mid 70s 
to around 80 degrees. The 00Z XMR skew-t sounding from last night 
indicates a substantial dry layer in the mid to upper levels. 
Additionally, analysis charts show a longwave ridge over the central 
and southern CONUS with 500mb heights at 594dm over the southern US. 
Meanwhile, high pressure (~1020mb) is over the eastern Gulf at the 
surface. 

High pressure will build over the eastern CONUS today with 500mb 
heights expected to reach the maximum percentile (598dm) for this 
time of year. Isolated to scattered showers (30-50% chance) and 
lightning storms are forecast to develop in the afternoon and 
evening as collisions occur between sea breezes and outflow from 
previous showers/lightning storms. Rain chances diminish by around 
8PM. Light and variable winds are forecast to turn onshore with the 
east coast sea breeze in the afternoon and evening at around 5-10mph 
today. Hi-res guidance shows MLCAPE up to 2,000-4,000 J/kg, 0-6km 
shear up to 10-30kts, conditionally unstable mid level lapse rates, 
and PWATs up to 1.80- 2.20" this afternoon. The aforementioned 
weather parameters are favorable for isolated strong storms capable 
of frequent lightning, wind gusts up to 30-50mph, and heavy rainfall 
(up to 1-3"). A hot and humid day is expected today with afternoon 
highs generally in the mid to upper 90s. Additionally, a Heat 
Advisory has been issued for all of east central Florida from 10AM 
to 8PM for heat index values up to 108-112F degrees. Remember to 
take frequent breaks from the heat, drink plenty of fluids, wear 
light colored clothing, and shift outdoor work away from the hottest 
parts of the day between the hours of 10am to 4pm. Above normal (2-
4+ degrees) lows in mid 70s to near 80F degrees are forecast 
overnight.

The Weekend... A persistent weather pattern is expected as the 
mid/upper level high with 500mb heights at 598dm expected to build 
over the eastern CONUS and the state of Florida. The high is then 
expected to shift west-southwest over the southwestern US on Sunday. 
Below normal rain chances are forecast through the weekend with high 
pressure over the region, as well as a Saharan Dust layer. Isolated 
to scattered showers (20-40% chance) and lightning storms are 
forecast to develop as collisions occur between sea breezes and 
outflow from previous showers/lightning storms with the greatest 
chance for showers and lightning storms generally south of Lake 
Kissimmee to Melbourne. High instability, low bulk shear, and 
sufficient PWATs suggests that there is the potential for isolated 
strong storms capable of frequent lightning, wind gusts up to 30-
50mph, and heavy rainfall (1-3") on Saturday. Even drier air is 
expected to advect over east central Florida on Sunday with a low 
chance (20%) for showers and lightning storms generally north of 
Melbourne to Kissimmee Prairie Preserve. Hot and humid conditions 
will continue with afternoon highs in the low to mid 90s along the 
coast and the mid to upper 90s inland. Additional Heat Advisories 
are likely with heat index values up to 108F to 112F degrees 
forecast. There is a widespread Major to Extreme HeatRisk (north of 
the Treasure Coast) for east central Florida each day. An extreme 
HeatRisk affects anyone without adequate cooling and hydration. Go 
to wcp.ncep.noaa.gov/heatrisk more information on HeatRisk. 

Monday-Thursday... Below normal rain chances are forecast to 
continue into at least the beginning of the work week. Ensembles, 
LREF-clusters, and deterministic models continue to be in decent 
agreement that the mid/upper level ridge will shift west-southwest 
over the southern US as a mid/upper trough deepens over the 
northeastern US. However, the latest model guidance does not deepen 
the trough as far south as previous model runs until later in the 
week and LREF-clusters, as well as deterministic models begin to 
diverge in different scenarios on Thursday. At the surface, a 
frontal boundary is forecast to sag over the eastern CONUS and 
southern US Tuesday into Wednesday which will result in an increase 
in rain chances over east central Florida. The heat wave is expected 
to continue with significant heat impacts for east central Florida. 
Afternoon highs in the mid to upper 90s are forecast with lows in 
the mid 70s to around 80 degrees. A Major HeatRisk is likely for 
most of east central Florida with the probabilities for an Extreme 
Heat Risk up to 30-70% mainly north of the Treasure Coast.
